domain: charity regulation / annual reporting deadline compliance (per-charity lodgment timeliness)
prediction_question: For an Australian charity registered with the ACNC that lodged its Annual Information Statement (AIS) for the reporting period ending in year Y-1 early enough that the lodgment was already recorded 90 days before its next deadline, will the charity FAIL to lodge its period-Y AIS by the ACNC-recorded due date for that period (the AIS 'date ais received' falls after the 'ais due date', or the charity never lodges a period-Y AIS and no row exists in the period-Y AIS dataset)?
prediction_time: Per-charity instant T = (the publisher-recorded 'ais due date' for the charity's period-Y AIS) minus 90 days. The due date is fixed by policy at six months after the reporting-period end (ACNC due-dates page), with the Commissioner's standing extension for standard 1 July-30 June periods to the following 31 January recorded in-file (measured: period ends 30/06/2023 carry due date 31/01/2024; 31/12/2024 carry 30/06/2025). Eligibility: the charity's period-(Y-1) AIS row exists with 'date ais received' <= T, and the charity is not listed as a member of an ACNC reporting group for period Y (group members lodge via their head entity; measured 2024: only 5 of 1,315 group-member ABNs also carry an individual period-2024 AIS row). All features come from the period-(Y-1) and earlier AIS datasets (finances, staffing, charity size, reporting-period structure, past lodgment timing including prior lateness) and the ACNC Register dataset; the target period-Y 'date ais received' (and row absence) is the label source and is excluded from features. Example instant (Australia/Sydney, AEDT): T = 2 November 2024 for a charity with FY ending 30/06/2024 (due 31/01/2025).
target_definition: Binary label 1 = charity fails to lodge its period-Y AIS by the due date, computed from the publisher's own recorded fields in the period-Y AIS dataset: label 1 iff ('date ais received' > 'ais due date') OR (no row for the ABN in the period-Y dataset as of the snapshot). Label 0 iff 'date ais received' <= 'ais due date'. Label source columns: 'date ais received' and row presence (both excluded from shipped features; 'ais due date' is a legitimate feature because it is determined by the period end and announced deadline policy, known before T). The label matches the ACNC's own compliance KPI ('Percentage of ... Annual Information Statements submitted by the due date', Annual Report 2025-26 KPI 1.3: 76% for 2025, 73% for 2024) against measured on-time shares of 73.96% (2023 file) and 74.95% (2024 file).

If the ACNC has approved for the information to be withheld, it won't appear in these datasets from the date of approval onwards.' - the recorded mechanism for the withheld-record label-noise channel.
split_strategy: Temporal windows on the target reporting-period year Y (periods ending in that calendar year; windows disjoint by Y). Candidate partition measured on the eligibility frame (prior AIS received <= T, group members excluded in construction): train Y in {2020, 2021}: 77,357 eligible rows / 23,205 positives (30.0%) / 54,152 negatives; eval {2022, 2023}: 80,977 / 20,958 (25.9%) / 60,019; holdout {2024}: 42,885 / 11,035 (25.7%) / 31,850. Both classes present in every window and every single year (per-year positive rates 25.7%-31.0%). Positives are spread across tens of thousands of distinct charities per year (eligible frames 37,970-42,885), not event clusters; a charity can appear in multiple target years, so per-charity clustering is a documented property for interval construction. XLSX-only years 2013-2018 can extend the train window at construction (worker parses XLSX; schema differences documented).

measurements.status_coding_measured: The AIS datasets carry a reason-coded 'registration status' on every historical row, distinguishing compliance outcomes from voluntary exit: 2024 mix (54,145 rows): Registered 52,274; 'Voluntarily Revoked No Longer Operating' 1,500; 'Voluntarily Revoked Merged' 175; 'Revoked Double Defaulter' 126; other revoked codes 70. Of the 1,935 prior-year filers absent from the 2024 file, 1,035 (53.5%) carry a 'Voluntarily Revoked*' code, 49+ are 'Revoked Double Defaulter' (the ACNC's own non-lodgment outcome), and 812 were still 'Registered' in the 2023-file snapshot (FY-end changes, pending extreme-late lodgment, or later revocation) - the frame-defining mixture at construction
measurements.group_reporting_measured: 2024 group-members file: 1,315 member ABNs (columns: ACNC group name, member ABN, member name, membership start/end dates); only 5 of them also carry an individual period-2024 AIS row (60 in the 2023 file, 242 in 2019 - members that once lodged individually). Group members must be excluded from the eligible frame; the exclusion is derivable from the published per-year group-members files
measurements.due_date_policy_measured: Offset from period end to recorded due date: 2024 file +7 months for 31,454 rows (all June-end periods, Commissioner-extended 31 January deadline) and +6 months for 14,127 (December-end, 30 June deadline); 2019 file +7 for 25,042 and +8 for 10,794 (May-end periods). The publisher's own 'ais due date' field is the operative deadline and varies with announced extensions - the label must use the recorded field, never a fixed rule
publisher_cross_checks: ACNC Annual Report 2025-26 KPI 1.3 'Percentage of 2025 Annual Information Statements submitted by the due date (Target: 75%, Result: 76%)'; 'At 30 June 2026, 76% of charities had submitted their Annual Information Statement by the due date, a significant improvement compared to 73% in the previous year' - consistent with measured on-time shares 74.95% (2024 file) and 73.96% (2023 file), small differences explained by the ACNC's fixed census date vs the final weekly-updated file

Australian Charities Report 11th edition: '52,627 Annual Information Statements ... for the 2023 reporting period ... 52,314 statements submitted by individual charities' and '313 Group Annual Information Statements submitted on behalf of 1,281 registered charities' vs 53,548 rows in the final 2023 file - a measured +1,234 rows after the report's census, quantifying the weekly trickle channel (late lodgers keep being added); the label is stable under trickle because a later-received period-Y AIS still has 'date ais received' after the past due date
known_event_fixtures: Deadline-extension fixture (verified in-file): charities with period ending 30/06/2023 carry 'ais due date' 31/01/2024 (seven months, the Commissioner's standing 31 January extension for standard-FY charities announced on the ACNC due-dates page), while period ending 31/12/2024 carries 30/06/2025 (six months, the nominal rule)

Dated example (real, verified from the fetched files; instants in Australia/Sydney, AEDT UTC+11): Integricare Limited, ABN 11000073870, FY 1 July-30 June. Feature row: period 01/07/2022-30/06/2023, recorded due date 31/01/2024, 'date ais received' 18/01/2024 (on time, lodgment observable before the instant). Target period: 01/07/2023-30/06/2024, recorded due date 31/01/2025. Prediction instant T = 31/01/2025 minus 90 days = 02/11/2024 (eligibility satisfied: prior AIS received 18/01/2024 <= T). Target window: lodgment in (02/11/2024, 31/01/2025]. Observed outcome: 'date ais received' 03/02/2025 > 31/01/2025 -> label 1 (failed to lodge by the due date, by 3 days). No part of the target window precedes T
vintage_caveats: AIS datasets are 'updated weekly' (ACNC download page) and the register 'regularly updated': the files fetched 2026-10-31 are one vintage per year, not archived snapshots; a construction snapshot date must be pinned and recorded. The 2023->2024 trickle is measured (+1,234 post-census rows via the Charities Report cross-check)

Withheld records are removed 'from the date of approval onwards' (ACNC register page): a charity that lodged on time but later won withholding would show as absent -> false positive. Mechanism recorded; rate not measurable from the current files; direction bounded (can only add positives, never remove them). publicdata.au rehosts the register dataset with version history (HF 'National-Digital/acnc-register' card) - a possible historical-vintage channel for register attributes, unverified for the AIS files

'registration status' on historical rows is current-vintage (status as of the last weekly update), not status-at-lodgment; using it for eligibility must be done at construction under the prediction-contract gate (a 'Voluntarily Revoked*' exclusion is post-hoc and must be declared; a 'Revoked Double Defaulter' exclusion would remove true positives and must not be used as an exclusion)

Schema drift: 2019 file has 167 columns including address/state and activity/beneficiary flags; 2020-2024 files (91-97 columns) drop address - location features for recent years come only from the register (current-vintage) or must be dropped; per-year 'Explanatory notes' PDFs are the publisher's column documentation

review: Five contracts reconciled on measured evidence. (1) Redistribution: every input dataset carries an explicit CC BY licence (per-year variants recorded) - class A; attribution conditions carried to LICENSE.md. (2) Prediction timing: per-charity instant T = recorded due date - 90 days, example worked in Australia/Sydney with real timestamps (Integricare: T 02/11/2024, due 31/01/2025, received 03/02/2025); features are prior-period AIS content whose lodgment (hence observability) predates T by the eligibility rule; label columns excluded; vintage caveats (weekly updates, withheld-record removal, current-vintage status) recorded with the measured trickle and the bounded direction of the withheld channel - the as-of policy is current-vintage retrospective with pinned snapshot dates, to be probed at construction per the prediction-contract gate. (3) Target: publisher-recorded ('date ais received' vs 'ais due date' + absence), matching the ACNC's own KPI definition; censoring channels are publisher-coded (voluntary revocation status codes, group-membership files) and the residual mixture is measured (812 'Registered'-status absentees of 1,935 in 2023->2024) and declared part of the definition. (4) Split capacity: measured eligible-frame counts for disjoint windows train 2020-2021 (77,357 rows, 30.00% positive), eval 2022-2023 (80,977, 25.88%), holdout 2024 (42,885, 25.73%), both classes everywhere, positives spread over tens of thousands of charities. (5) Not a mirror: mechanical novelty search recorded; no ML-ready formulation of this or a sibling target exists externally; internal siblings target different outcomes (filing-population exit) in other jurisdictions. Uncertainty that remains: the withheld-record false-positive rate is unmeasured (mechanism recorded, direction bounded) and the 2013-2018 XLSX backfill for a longer train window is untested - both are construction-time, non-blocking.
next_action: CONSTRUCTION (advancement owns it; handoff order: construction -> full-worker qualification -> exact-byte acceptance -> reference/model scoring -> reporting). Construction step: on a worker, fetch the pinned-vintage CSVs for AIS years 2019-2024 (optionally XLSX 2013-2018 to extend train), build the (ABN, target-year) panel with the eligibility frame (prior AIS received <= due-90d; group members excluded via the per-year group-members files), label = failed-to-lodge-by-recorded-due-date, features from prior AIS rows + register attributes, splits train 2020-2021 / eval 2022-2023 / holdout 2024. Expected artifact: runner-contract train/eval/holdout CSVs (~77k/81k/43k rows). Deciding checks: dataset-qualification gate on the full artifact (leakage: label-source columns excluded; prediction-timing reverse-history probes for the eligibility and vintage assumptions per docs/PREDICTION-CONTRACT.md, including the due-date-announcement timing for the 31-January extension years), exact-byte acceptance, then the baseline triad (persistence/prior-lateness reference first - prior-year lateness is the natural dominant reference and must be measured).
